question: What are the core Customs Systems used by URA for trade facilitation and clearance?
answer: Published under Tax Education > General Tax Information > Customs Systems (https://ura.go.ug/en/category/tax-education/general-tax-information/customs-systems/): URA operates an integrated technological ecosystem to automate cross-border trade, customs valuation, transit cargo monitoring, and warehousing. Key core systems include: 1) ASYCUDA World (cargo declaration and processing); 2) Uganda Electronic Single Window (UESW, joint agency permits and licenses); 3) Regional Electronic Cargo Tracking System (RECTS, real-time satellite transit monitoring); 4) Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII, high-speed X-ray scanning); 5) Bonded Warehouse Information Management System (BWIMS, bonded inventory tracking); and 6) URA Touchpoint Portal for installers and system registration.

question: What is ASYCUDA World and how does it process customs declarations?
answer: Published on June 24, 2024 by Okao Brian (https://ura.go.ug/en/sycuda/), ASYCUDA World (Automated System for Customs Data) is an online web-based customs management system developed by UNCTAD. It handles 100% of Uganda's import, export, and transit declarations. Key functionalities: 1) Manifest submission: Shipping lines and air carriers lodge electronic manifests before vessel arrival; 2) Self-Declaration: Licensed clearing agents submit Single Administrative Documents (SAD / Form C17); 3) Automated Risk Selectivity: Routes declarations into Green (immediate auto-release), Blue (post-clearance audit), Yellow (documentary check by DPC), or Red (physical inspection); 4) Tax Assessment: Automatically computes import duty, VAT, excise duty, and environmental levies; 5) Electronic payment: Integrates with URA e-Tax to issue PRNs.

question: What was announced in the Urgent Notice to All Customs Clients regarding ASYCUDA World?
answer: Published on March 10, 2025 by Kamugisha Kabahweza Allan (https://ura.go.ug/en/urgent-notice-to-all-customs-clients/): URA officially announced that the ASYCUDA World Installer and Customs System Registration Forms are accessible through the URA Touchpoint Portal at https://touchpoint.ura.go.ug. All licensed customs clearing agents, importers, and shipping lines must download the modernized installer, update Java runtime configurations, and register their system access credentials via Touchpoint to maintain uninterrupted customs transaction processing.

question: What is the Uganda Electronic Single Window (UESW)?
answer: Published on June 24, 2024 by Okao Brian (https://ura.go.ug/en/uesw/): The Uganda Electronic Single Window (UESW) is a trade facilitation platform that enables international trade stakeholders to lodge standardized documentation with all relevant government agencies through a single entry point. Integrating over 20 Other Government Agencies (OGAs)—including UNBS, NDA, MAAIF, Ministry of Trade, and URA—it allows traders to apply for electronic permits, quality certificates, sanitary/phytosanitary clearances, and customs clearance simultaneously, reducing border dwell times from days to hours.

question: What is the Regional Electronic Cargo Tracking System (RECTS)?
answer: Published on June 24, 2024 by Okao Brian (https://ura.go.ug/en/rects/): RECTS is an integrated GPS/satellite-based electronic cargo tracking system operated jointly by revenue authorities across the Northern Corridor (Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda). Electronic smart seals are affixed to transit trucks and containerized cargo at Mombasa, Naivasha, or border points. Real-time monitoring from central control centers triggers automated alarms if there is route deviation from the 21 gazetted transit corridors, unauthorized stops, seal tampering, or door opening, eliminating transit diversion without requiring physical customs escorts.

question: What is Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII) in customs clearance?
answer: Published on June 21, 2024 by Sandra Kakooza (https://ura.go.ug/en/non-intrusive-inspection/): Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII) is the examination of cargo, containers, and passenger baggage using advanced radiographic imaging (drive-through and mobile X-ray scanners) without physically unpacking the consignment. Scans are completed in under one minute under strict Atomic Energy Council radiation safety protocols. NII identifies hidden contraband, uncustomed merchandise, and misdeclared cargo while expediting legitimate trade at border stations (Malaba, Busia, Mutukula, Mirama Hills, Katuna, Elegu, and Entebbe Airport).

question: What is the Bonded Warehouse Information Management System (BWIMS)?
answer: Published on June 21, 2024 by Sandra Kakooza (https://ura.go.ug/en/bwims/): BWIMS is a digital inventory tracking and management system designed under the Domestic Revenue Mobilization Strategy (DRMS) to monitor goods in all licensed private and public customs bonded warehouses. It tracks cargo in real-time from receipt under the IM7 regime to storage, internal movement, and final release under IM4 (home consumption) or re-export. BWIMS reconciles stock balances automatically with Asycuda World and ensures strict enforcement of statutory warehousing time limits.

question: What are the rules for clearance and removal of goods in customs warehouses at Naivasha ICD and Mombasa Port?
answer: Published on August 5, 2026 by Kamugisha Kabahweza Allan (https://ura.go.ug/en/clearance-removal-of-goods-in-the-customs-warehouse-naivasha-and-at-the-mombasa-port/): Pursuant to Section 42(1) of EACCMA 2004, the Commissioner of Customs requires all cargo owners with goods stored at the Naivasha Inland Container Depot (ICD) and Mombasa Port beyond statutory limits to clear duties and remove goods immediately. Failure to clear within thirty (30) days of public notice leads to forfeiture and disposal via public online auction (singlewindow.go.ug/auction) or private treaty direct sale.
